It moves beyond standard technical, economic, or policy descriptions and instead appeals to an ethical framework detailing how individuals or institutions ought to behave based on moral criteria.","clarification":"To classify a text as containing moral rhetoric, look for: (1) Explicit mentions of core values or virtues (e.g., 'respect,' 'courage,' 'patriotism,' 'caring'). (3) Moral condemnations of bad societal states or actions (e.g., 'not tolerable,' 'unfairly discriminate,' 'corruption'). Even if the policy has an underlying social utility (e.g., improving roads or expanding schools), it does not count as moral rhetoric unless the phrasing relies on value-laden moral concepts or ethical duties.
